description: The relay queue uses write-to-tmp then rename for both .msg and .env, writes .msg before .env (so the drain only sees complete pairs), and runs cleanup_tmp_files + cleanup_orphan_msg_files on startup. This correctly handles all crash windows: crash mid-enqueue leaves only a .tmp (deleted on restart) or only a .msg without .env (moved to dead/). A future contributor might suggest simplifying to direct writes — this must be resisted: direct writes are not atomic and create a window where the drain could attempt to deliver a partial message. The ordering (.msg first) is also load-bearing: drain scans for .env files as the trigger; missing .msg is handled gracefully.
title: Relay queue crash-safety design: atomic tmp→rename, .msg-before-.env, orphan cleanup
